newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA STALS SAYS HOPEFUL OF RATE CUT BY END '97.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA STALS SAYS HOPEFUL OF RATE CUT BY END '97.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday he was hopeful of a relaxation in monetary policy before the end of this year.
Stals told state radio that he was encouraged by the latest money supply, inflation and trade data which were released earlier this week.
"I think the money supply rate of change, the rate of inflation and also the trade statistics are all moving in the right direction at this stage," he said.

"The influence of last year's depreciation (of the rand) is working itself out from the inflation now, so I think all the indicators tell us that we are moving in the right direction and hopefully before the end of this year we will be in a position to relax on the monetary policy."

On Monday, the central bank released data showing money supply growth slowed to a preliminary 12.79 percent rise in June from 15.32 percent in May and bank credit extension growth up 16.39 percent from 16.65 percent in June.

That was followed on Tuesday by Central Statistics data showing annual inflation at a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June and Customs and Excise data showing South Africa's trade balance swelled to 4.15 billion rand in the same month from 1.75 billion rand in May.
Economists were dismayed by the private sector credit data, which they said dampened prospects of a near-term rate cut.
"One must not make too much out of one statistic...especially not on a monthly basis," Stals said.
"But it is a little bit of a disappointment that the rate of increase in bank credit extension is not slowing down as most of the other indicators tell us at this stage," he added.

"In the final situation the increase in bank credit still creates more money and more money can hold a danger for inflation in future so we have to be careful about relaxing the monetary policy too soon."
Asked to predict when the country could expect a reduction in interest rates, Stals said:

"I think the financial markets are too volatile and too unpredictable. We just think that (with) the amounts of capital that flow into the country and out of the country one must be very careful about the predictions we make," Stals said.
